principle: A status describes the kind and strength of support a claim currently has in this repository. It never means 'true'. Machine-checkable parts are enforced by substrate/epistemic.py; tests/test_epistemic_guards.py verifies the enforcement.

statuses.meaning: Adopted by definition or convention for this research (e.g. Sigma={0,1}). Not evidence-bearing; can be changed only by an ontology change record.
Accepted in the relevant external discipline and traceable to a cited source or to a standard derivation.
Follows from definitions by an argument written down in this repository (evidence_sources.json, kind=derivation). Computation may corroborate but does not replace the argument.
Measured from something that exists independently of the instrument: physical hardware or this repository's recorded history. Executing a model never yields OBSERVED.
statuses.requires: evidence with domain physical or repository

statuses.meaning: Produced by executing a computational model. True of the model under its configuration; says nothing about any system the model stands in for.
statuses.requires: evidence with domain computational or simulated and a run_id

statuses.meaning: A pre-registered falsification condition was evaluated and not triggered, in a run that has been reproduced (>=2 executions with identical deterministic hash). Scope is the subject domain of the evidence: model-only evidence supports claims about the model only.
statuses.requires: falsification stated and checked; reproduced run; for physical claims, physical evidence

statuses.meaning: Supported by an external source whose exact supporting proposition is recorded; not independently checked here.
Reasoned from other recorded evidence without direct test. The strongest status an interpretation can carry.
statuses.requires: non-interpretive evidence it is inferred from

statuses.meaning: A working position adopted to make progress (a naming or modelling choice), explicitly open to revision.
A testable proposition that has not yet been tested.
statuses.requires: a statement and, ideally, a falsification condition

statuses.meaning: Cannot currently be tested or the evidence is inconclusive/contradictory.
A falsification condition was triggered or a counterexample was recorded. Preserved, never deleted.
Withdrawn for non-empirical reasons (ill-posed, redundant with established theory, misleading terminology). Preserved with rationale.

forbidden: PROVEN (use DERIVED for mathematics, EXPERIMENTALLY_SUPPORTED for tests)
'novel' without a novelty_scope in {repository, team, literature_unsearched, literature_searched}

evidence_domains.computational: execution of a model that is itself the subject of the claim
evidence_domains.simulated: execution of a model standing in for another target (e.g. injected flips standing in for physical upsets)
evidence_domains.repository: measurement of this repository's own recorded history

novelty_scopes.repository: not previously present in this repository
novelty_scopes.team: not previously known to the people/agents working here
novelty_scopes.literature_searched: a recorded literature search did not find it (still not a proof of scientific novelty)
